title: EFC Validation: Cluster Lensing and Galaxy Rotation Curves
abstract_short: EFC passes both cluster lensing (Bullet Cluster) and galaxy rotation curve tests. Gas term statistically irrelevant (p=0.99). Rotation χ²=4.5 vs Newton χ²=296.

lambda_scaling.interpretation: λ scales with system size, not universal constant

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: A new empirical-validation paper has been deposited that targets cross-scale EFC checks: cluster lensing (including Bullet Cluster) and galaxy rotation curves (SPARC), framed via entropy coupling and λ scaling. With no sealed predictions or declared kill criteria in the manuscript metadata and no extracted quantitative results yet, this primarily seeds a set of planned tests and a joint-consistency harness tying cluster lensing to rotation curves. If its results confirm a single coupling law across these regimes, it would materially strengthen EFC’s cross-scale consistency, but for now it adds planned tests without closing any KC or gap.
graph_insights: The paper creates a new bridge in the graph between the SPARC node and cluster-lensing/Bullet-Cluster nodes via the λ-scaling and entropy-coupling concepts, where no prior validation tests were recorded.
Absence of linked sealed predictions or prior related DOIs indicates this is a new spoke in the validation network rather than an update to an existing branch.

tests_added.name: Bullet Cluster lensing under EFC entropy coupling (no collisionless DM component)
tests_added.description: Evaluate whether EFC’s entropy-coupled potential reproduces the observed weak/strong lensing mass maps and galaxy–gas offsets in the Bullet Cluster without invoking a collisionless dark matter halo.
tests_added.data_source: HST/ACS weak+strong lensing reconstructions; Chandra X-ray gas maps; ground-based shear catalogs
tests_added.prediction: Structural: Lensing convergence peaks and offsets can be accounted for by baryons (galaxies + ICM) through the entropy-coupled potential, with scaling governed by the EFC λ-law.

tests_added.name: SPARC rotation curves with single-parameter λ-scaling
tests_added.description: Test whether a single λ-scaling relation (potential coupling to baryonic surface density/entropy proxy) explains the flat rotation curves across the SPARC sample with low residuals and predictable trends.
tests_added.data_source: SPARC database (HI/Hα rotation curves and 3.6 μm photometry)
tests_added.prediction: Structural: Rotation curves follow a universal coupling law between baryonic distribution and effective potential; residuals track gas fraction/entropy proxies as prescribed by EFC.

tests_added.name: Cross-scale λ and entropy-coupling consistency: clusters vs. galaxies
tests_added.description: Jointly fit the EFC entropy-coupling function and λ-normalization to SPARC rotation curves and cluster lensing profiles; test if one coupling law applies across galaxy and cluster scales within uncertainties.
tests_added.data_source: SPARC + cluster lensing datasets (e.g., CLASH, HSC, XMM/Chandra ICM thermodynamics)
tests_added.prediction: Structural: The same entropy-coupling function and λ-normalization (or explicitly prescribed environment dependence) reproduce both rotation curves and cluster shear/convergence profiles.

ledger_impact.bottom_line_sentence: Paper deposited (10.6084/m9.figshare.31190233) defining cross-scale lensing–rotation-curve tests under EFC entropy coupling/λ scaling; tests registered and pending extraction/verification of quantitative results.
implicit_consequences: Triggers a unified likelihood pipeline tying SPARC rotation curves to cluster shear/convergence profiles under a single coupling law.
Requires defining and standardizing entropy proxies (e.g., surface density, gas fraction, ICM thermodynamics) consistently across galaxy and cluster regimes.
Enables a single-parameter (λ) cross-scale constraint that can tighten EFC parameter space even before DESI DR2 RSD arrives.
Motivates curation of Bullet Cluster-quality datasets for multiple merging clusters to generalize beyond a single system.
